$$\boxed{D+C_0\le H.}

A terminal claim also determines its original leg.Each original corner can receive at most one claim. Its physical canonical tile and its original positive pair are fixed; two distinct parent bar pairs in that tile would overlap original endpoints.Each original terminal can receive at most one claim. $$C_1\le A,\qquad E_1\le A.

$$\boxed{B\le 2A+H.}$$

$$2R=A+U_0+Z_0+H,$$

or, more precisely,
$$\boxed{B+H+2U_0+2Z_0\le4R.}

$$H=X=0,\qquad A=2,$$
and the two activated original positive legs are precisely the short legs of the two width-six doubles.4.1 A counted corner cannot charge an AA terminalReturn to the full-receiver configuration with

If  $x$  were an activated short terminal of an AA positive, its original blank toward the other positive leg would be  $b$ .But for the normalized AA source  $O=U(6,a,b_0)$ , the accepted short-gate owner has near stem
$$\{(r,5):2\le r\le k+2\},
\qquad k\ge b_0.$$
It therefore owns the inward neighbor  $(b_0,5)$  of the activated short tip  $(b_0,6)$ . $$\boxed{B\le A=2.}
\tag{9}$$

$$O=U(6,a,b),$$
with the right short leg activated. Its short outer corner is  $(0,6)$ .In these coordinates, the charging phase10 source  $F$  has:

\text{bar rows }-1,\ldots,v-2,$$
and its legs point east.Write the accepted short-gate owner as
$$\mathcal R(r,c)=(k+2-r,c+4).$$

$$v\le k+2.$$
The accepted four-stem inequalities give  $k\le a-10$ , so
$$\boxed{v\le k+2\le a-8.}
\tag{10}$$
This compares the negative owner’s width with the positive owner’s long height. $$O_L(r,c)=(7-c,2+r),
\qquad
O_R(r,c)=(7-c,v-1-r).$$

$$[2,a_L+2],
\qquad
[v-1-a_R,v-1].$$

\tag{11}$$

An unbounded restriction on closed neutral U-port componentsThe preceding result can be converted into an embedded-curve invariant.Consider the graph with:one vertex for each relevant original phase01 or phase10 U;the two original terminal  $1P1T$  ports of a phase01 U;the two original outer-corner  $1P1T$  ports of a phase10 U;an edge when two such ports share an actual nonfull  $2P1T$  receiver.Consider a closed component in which every port is paired within this graph. Other contacts of these sources are allowed; this is a graph of specified ports, not an assumption that the entire endpoint contact graph is a cycle.Call a port active when its original blank is filled and its original support remains selected. Call it passive when its original support is consumed and its original blank remains unoccupied. Each neutral edge has exactly one active and one passive end.5.1 The embedded curve and its turning numberWithin each phase01 source, connect its two ports along its original stems and outer bar. Within each phase10 source, connect them along its original outer bar.These are simple arcs of original endpoints. Different original sources have disjoint endpoint sets. Adding the unit contact edges gives a simple closed lattice curve for each closed port component.At a port let: $s$  point into its source arc; $d$  point toward its unique original blank; $\chi=\det(s,d)\in\{-1,1\}$ .Across an active-to-passive contact  $p\to q=p+d$ ,
$$(s_q,d_q)=(d_p,-s_p).$$
Thus  $\chi$  is preserved across a contact and changes sign across each source. The cycle has an even number of sources.Orient the cycle. Let  $u_i=1$  for phase01 and  $u_i=0$  for phase10, and let  $\beta_i=1$  if the exit port is active and  $-1$  if it is passive.A phase01 source arc contributes  $2\chi_i$  quarter-turns; a phase10 source arc contributes zero. The contact contributes  $\chi_i\beta_i$ . Consequently,
$$\sum_i\chi_i(2u_i+\beta_i)=\pm4.
\tag{14}$$
This is the ordinary total-turn identity for a simple orthogonal closed curve.5.2 The AA restriction changes the possible cycle balanceBy (13), a passive phase10 port forces its owner’s other receiver to be full. Hence a phase10 source on a closed neutral component must have both ports active.Let  $a_i$  be the number of active ports of source  $i$ . On an oriented cycle,
$$a_i=1+\frac{\beta_i-\beta_{i-1}}2.$$
Using the alternating signs  $\chi_i$ , equation (14) becomes, in AA,
$$\pm4=\sum_{i:\,01}\chi_i a_i.
\tag{15}$$
Every edge contributes exactly one active port. If the component has  $m_{01}$  phase01 and  $m_{10}$  phase10 owners, port balance therefore gives
$$\sum_{i:\,01}a_i=m_{01}-m_{10}.
\tag{16}$$
Taking absolute values in (15),
$$\boxed{m_{01}-m_{10}\ge4.}$$
There is also a useful source/sink restriction. Let  $p,q,m$  count phase01 owners with two, zero, and one active ports, respectively. Since all phase10 owners have two active ports, port balance gives
$$q=p+m_{10}.$$
Equation (15) can be rewritten as
$$\pm4=
\sum_{01\text{ double-active}}\chi
-\sum_{01\text{ double-passive}}\chi
-\sum_{10}\chi.$$
Its absolute value is at most
$$p+q+m_{10}=2q.$$
Therefore
$$\boxed{q\ge2.}
\tag{17}$$
Every closed neutral component must contain at least two original phase01 owners with both ports passive. For a pure phase01 component, at least two owners are double-active and at least two are double-passive.Across  $\ell$  different closed port components, owners and ports do not repeat, so
$$\boxed{m_{01,\mathrm{total}}-m_{10,\mathrm{total}}\ge4\ell.}
\tag{18}$$
These are actual ownership counts. They do not become reserve merely by counting their negative charges:  $C-K_{\rm irregular}$  remains part of  $R$ . What remains to closeThe new shared contribution is (1). Its AA consequences are stronger than a count of distinct split points:every counted corner injects into one of the two actual activated short legs;at most two such corners exist globally;a counted phase10 corner forces that owner’s other receiver to be full;closed U-only neutral port components require the excess and source/sink structure in (18) and (17).The unresolved transfer is now more specific.
